title: Rework icon-button hit area and progressive-loading escape hatch
creator: Claire Nguyen
description: This ticket addresses three interrelated button regressions observed in the last token migration: (1) icon-only buttons with dense layouts lost tappable area consistency across platforms, (2) the current loading affordance causes layout shift and is not cancelable (blocking quick user recovery), and (3) high-contrast/dark-theme token fallbacks produce poor disabled-state contrast. Goal: define a stable interaction layer spec and a progressive-loading "escape hatch" pattern that is accessible, non-shifting, token-friendly, and implementable by engineering with minimal runtime branching.
acceptance_criteria: Icon-only buttons have a minimum 44px tap target across all densities without shifting existing visual alignment

The loading affordance for icon and compact buttons is non-blocking: an overlay spinner shows after a short debounce (150ms) and can be cancelled by a subsequent action from the user or replaced by a small inline skeleton after 800ms
ARIA semantics: buttons expose aria-busy during active loading and aria-live notifications only for cancellation/timeout events; assistive tech receives concise status updates
Disabled visual tokens map to new semantic tokens with at least 3:1 contrast (or a documented exception with compensating measures) in both light and dark high-contrast themes
Design tokens include fallback mappings for legacy components to avoid runtime regressions during the rollout
Implementation guide and code examples (React/vanilla) submitted and merged by ENG with an accompanying unit test and a visual regression baseline
engineering_notes: ENG spike (ENG-8420) measured event latency distributions — 95th percentile ~380ms for compact routes; debounce set at 150ms to avoid flash
Plan: implement spinner overlay as absolutely positioned element that does not affect layout; progressive fallback to inline skeleton after 800ms to indicate longer-running work
Token migration: add semantic token aliases --button-on, --button-disabled, --icon-button-hitpad and publish migration map; engineering to accept legacy aliases for 2 cycles
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/1827 (WIP) — includes storybook examples and automated axe checks
QA: visual-regression screenshots and an accessibility audit checklist (voiceover + TalkBack) required prior to merge

2026-02-25 UX Research: Quick moderated test with 8 participants — cancellation affordance (tap a second time to cancel) preferred over a dedicated cancel button for icon-only actions. Added accessibility note to expose cancellation to assistive tech.

2026-03-05 Aisha Patel: Updated Figma with new hitpad overlays and added states for delayed load >800ms. Included compact skeleton and labelled components for token audit.
2026-03-08 Eng review (PR feedback): Left comments about CSS specificity and suggested using CSS custom properties for toggling spinner color per token rather than hardcoded HEX values.
